title: Swift
subtitle: A safe, fast, expressive compiled language: from your first program to value types, protocols, Swift 6 concurrency and the apps built with it.
description: Swift is a general-purpose compiled language that Apple announced in 2014 and open-sourced in 2015. It is the main language for apps on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV and Apple Vision Pro, and it also runs on Linux and Windows, where people use it for servers, command-line tools and, increasingly, embedded devices. Its designers name three goals, and the course keeps returning to them: code should be safe by default, run fast, and read clearly.

This course is for anyone who knows what a variable, a loop and a function are, for example from the [Start level of Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience. It goes from installing the toolchain and printing a first line to optionals, value and reference types, enums with associated values, protocols and generics, typed errors and tests, memory management with ARC, and the data-race safety of Swift 6, and it ends with a complete project. App frameworks such as SwiftUI and UIKit are described, but every program you run here uses only the standard library, so it works on any operating system.

To run the code, install the official toolchain from [swift.org/install](https://www.swift.org/install/) (Xcode on a Mac also includes it). There is no official online playground; Apple's free [Swift Playgrounds](https://www.apple.com/swift/playgrounds/) app runs Swift on an iPad or Mac. Every complete program in these lessons was compiled with `swiftc` from Swift 6.4 on Linux and run, and its output is shown exactly as it printed.

levels.title: The core language
levels.summary: Install the toolchain and learn the everyday language: constants and types, strings and collections, control flow and switch, and the optionals that keep missing values honest.

levels.title: Modelling with types
levels.summary: Write functions and closures, choose between structs, classes and enums, and build abstractions with protocols, extensions and generics.

levels.title: Swift as professionals write it
levels.summary: Typed errors and tests, memory management with ARC, async/await and actors under Swift 6 data-race safety, how apps for Apple platforms are made, and a complete project.
